subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Safest Cars Ever Tested
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Safest Cars Ever Tested.

hook.text: Some brands have built reputations entirely around one word—safety.

buildup.text: Volvo pledged in 2020 that no one would die in a new Volvo, setting a bold public goal.

discovery.text: Subaru's EyeSight system helped its cars achieve some of the lowest crash injury rates on record.

twist.text: The safest cars aren't always the priciest—several affordable models earn top scores.

climax.text: Tesla's Model 3 recorded the lowest probability of injury ever measured in NHTSA testing.

punchline.text: Safety leaders prove that protecting lives sells cars.

quiz.question: Which brand publicly pledged zero deaths in its new cars?

details.summary: A handful of modern vehicles have achieved near-perfect scores across every crash test category, demonstrating how far engineering has advanced in protecting occupants from every angle of impact.
details.whyItMatters: Top-rated cars set benchmarks for the entire industry. When one manufacturer achieves outstanding results, competitors must follow, continuously ratcheting up the baseline of vehicle safety.
takeaways: Some models score maximums in frontal, side, and rollover tests
Advanced driver-assist features boost overall safety ratings
Safety leaders often pioneer features that later become standard

faq.question: Which cars consistently rank among the safest ever tested?
faq.answer: Volvo, Subaru, and Tesla models frequently appear at the top of safety rankings. The Tesla Model Y and Volvo XC90 have both earned exceptional marks across multiple international testing programs.

faq.question: Does a safer car always cost more to buy?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Several affordable models like the Honda Civic and Mazda3 earn top safety ratings. Advanced safety features have trickled down to mainstream vehicles as component costs have decreased.
